subject: Inference cost vs fidelity tradeoffs & benchmark asks
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + what we can measure next (cost/fidelity routing tests)

Thanks again for the call this morning, Samantha — good discussion and clear priorities on your side. Quick recap and proposed next experiments so we can get you a defensible apples-to-apples comparison versus your hyperscaler options.

Recap (what you emphasized):
- Tight 99th latency SLO for customer-facing hallucination-sensitive endpoints (~150–200ms target).
- Cost pressure: looking at per-1M token economics for high-volume routes (50M+ tokens/mo).
- Quality: willingness to trade some speed for higher response fidelity on top-tier routes.
- Operational constraints: KV cache persistence between requests and predictable throughput during launches.

What Redwood can measure for BrightLayer (proposed, low-effort checklist):
1) Per-1M token cost baseline at three batch sizes (1, 8, 32) using the same model family (we suggest open-llm-x-13b-quant as parity).
2) Cache-hit sensitivity: run 1M token pass with cold cache, 1M tokens warm (targeted 60% / 80% hit scenarios).
3) Routing tradeoff: route high-fidelity calls to full-precision variant with autoscaling vs cheap quantized variant; record delta in latency and cost.
4) Tail latency profile (p50/p90/p99) for each configuration with 95th percentile concurrency from your production estimates.

Deliverables: a one-page benchmark matrix, per-1M token cost table, and a recommended routing policy and default batching guidance. I attached the initial benchmark matrix template and a starter cost model for reference.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm which three endpoints you want us to test (IDs or example prompts)?
- Can procurement share any constraints (procurement@)? we may need an NDA for deeper log sharing.
- Would you like Redwood to run a 1M-token sample on your data in our sandboxes (we can scrub PII)?

If that all sounds right I’ll pull Ben and Neha in to scope the test run and schedule a 2–3 hour execution window next week.

Best,
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: benchmark-matrix-v1.xlsx, redwood-cost-model.csv
From: Samantha Li <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLayer Procurement <procure@brightlayer.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + what we can measure next (cost/fidelity routing tests)

Thanks, Markus — this is exactly the level of granularity we need. A few clarifications from our side before you run anything: 

1) Endpoints: Please use the public-search endpoint (search_v2), the summarization endpoint (summ_v1_high), and our chat-assist endpoint (assist_live). I can share example prompts for each in a follow-up.
2) Data: we prefer you run with synthetic prompts that mimic our distribution — I can send a 1k-sample set.
3) Procurement note: we need a light NDA before you ingest any production traces (procure@ copied). If you can share a standard mutual NDA link, procurement will get back to us within 48 hrs.

Also: how do you handle model substitutions during capacity fallbacks? We need a short note for our architecture team on fidelity degradation when routing to cheaper variants.

Samantha
Head of AI Platforms | BrightLayer
samantha@brightlayer.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + what we can measure next (cost/fidelity routing tests)

Samantha — thanks, that helps. Answers inline and execution plan below.

Model substitution and fidelity notes (short):
- Redwood ships model variants (full, quantized, and low-rank approximations). At routing time we classify requests by policy (cost-sensitive, fidelity-sensitive, or default).
- Fallbacks: when capacity or cost constraints kick in we route to the closest-compatible variant. We keep an automated fidelity checklist: key tokens, stop-sequence behavior, and a small eval suite of 50 prompts to detect degradation. If degradation exceeds your tolerance we automatically route back and notify.

Execution plan (proposed 1M-token run):
- Data: you send 1k synthetic prompts for each endpoint (search_v2, summ_v1_high, assist_live).
- Tests: 
  A) Baseline: full-precision variant, batch sizes [1, 8, 32], cold cache -> 250k tokens per endpoint (total ~750k).
  B) Cache-sensitivity sweep: for assist_live run warm-cache and cold-cache windows to simulate 60% and 80% hit rates (extra 250k tokens).
  C) Routing delta: run a 100k-token sample routing 10% of requests to cheaper quantized variant to estimate fidelity delta.
- Metrics collected: per-token cost, p50/p90/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio, and automated eval score (BLEU/ROUGE proxies we agreed on).

Logistics:
- I’m attaching an updated benchmark template with the exact columns Redwood will populate and a starter cost model (attached).
- NDA: Laura — can you share our standard mutual NDA link to Samantha/procurement? (Laura, looping you to expedite).

If BrightLayer signs the NDA we can run the synthetic samples this Thursday (no PII ingestion). Estimated turnaround for the report: 3 business days after the run completes.

Ben and Neha, please confirm resource availability for Thursday and whether we need to provision a dedicated pool or we can run on hosted tiers.

Thanks,
Markus

Attachments: benchmark-matrix-v1.xlsx (updated), redwood-cost-model.csv
